title: Uber Driver Sign-up Bonus: Extra $2,000 (100 Passenger Trips in 90 Days) / $500 (100 Deliveries in 60 Days) @ Uber
body:
Deal: Uber Driver Sign-up Bonus: Extra $2,000 (100 Passenger Trips in 90 Days) / $500 (100 Deliveries in 60 Days) @ Uber

[HappyJoyJoy] If you’ve got an EV, this might be worth looking at. If you’re using a petrol car, once you factor in fuel, servicing, tyres and depreciation, I probably wouldn’t bother just for the bonus.
[tessel] Don't forget insurance. If doing it properly you can't just use any insurance.
[prankster] Yeah what insurance coverage do you need?
[tenpercent] @prankster: So what insurance coverage is it that you want?
[MrZ] I remember when I first started doing Uber about 10 years ago, I rang RACV and they said my policy would cover "some" Uber but not full-time Uber. They wouldn't clarify exactly what that meant. Anyway I was using that coverage up until recently when I decided to be safe and officially tell them I was doing Uber. My premium went up by about $1,000 a year.
[iwantaphone] Don’t forget to pay the co-driver, they charge up to 47% including your sign up bonus 😉 they go by the name ATO or smth
[OZKap] Someone doing uber is not paying anywhere near 47% tax lmao
[dbnewman89] If I had an EV I'd give this a crack for the bonus $2k - few weekends should knock out 100 trips (Gold Coast), and my effective tax rate would be 38%…
[cloudy] Did uber increase driver pay or something during the petrol price spikes early this year? Or some sort of fuel levy slapped on riders that went to drivers?
[ATTS] Do u wait till last moment to pick up customers food btw?

[eltito] For me personally, if I was to sign up, it would only to obtain the bonus by meeting the minimum requirements
[welcomeUniverseWorld] Your car insurance likely will go up if you are doing this for the first time
[urbancartel] @eltito: your car registration will also be changed to commercial vehicle meaning your warranty is now reduced to whatever the manufacturer states (typically 150,000 ks) even if you only do it for long enough to get this bonus
[bruhminister] Not just insurance. There's multiple accreditations and road checks and rego for a commercial vehicle. Plus you pay 30% income tax and gst and pay your accountant to create a gst number for you.
So yeah, nah. Not worth it.
[Dyl] Some regional areas you can get pickups in minutes
Uber eats isn’t too congested

Rideshare

[evocable] Uber is at least half of what a taxi costs and sometimes 1/3 if the taxi driver decides to just charge whatever he wants. Legit had nothing but horrendous experiences with taxis at Perth airport - third world country vibes with them not using meters, no ID visible, charging double what it normally costs. I'll only ever take Uber or Didi now, even though I have to wait longer and that's with my employer footing the bill…
[meowsers] @evocable: I've had taxis try to scam me both in SYD and PER and it's actually quite enjoyable to call them out on it. Now admittedly if i was female or not from here I would be worried but actually telling them to STFU takes away from the annoyance of getting scammed.
Basically you can always refuse to pay. On the other end when they have tried the maxitaxi scam, or the eftpos machine scam, or in SYD refusing a flat fare .. it works every time. I just play confused, refuse to pay, and get out of the taxi. Has only happened 3 times in 3 years but still.
I would suggest starting a video, taking a photo (with the flash to prove a point) and then taking a pic of their rego. Make sure you get your luggage first of course…
[Onemoredeal] Uber wouldn’t even exist if taxis had provided a decent product and didn’t constantly refuse fares and rip people off
[Sfh1975] @Onemoredeal: It did not start with a social goal in mind but yes, it has managed to keep existing due to poor taxi services.
[Hvrd] for future people seeing it, unless you can see the challenge in the promo tab its not going to happen
[DingoBlue] Thanks. Can you see the promo tab before going through the whole rigmarole of signing up?
[ozbdssll] You won't be able to see the in-app promo tab until your account and docs are fully approved, but as long as you sign up directly through the referral link, the offer is automatically attached to your application.
The referral landing page spells out the full Terms & Conditions (the required number of trips, deadline, and reward amount) right before you submit your details.
Just make sure to take a quick screenshot of that referral page and the T&Cs when you register for peace of mind, just in case Uber support ever asks for it later.
[makeyouryear] They did this to me as well. Targeted offer directly in the app and I first confirmed my eligibility for the promo with support too. Once the challenge was completed they said I'd signed up many years earlier. From what I can tell I sent an email with Q's about driving for uber 7 years earlier. I didn't have a full licence at that time, in their words I could "sign-up" once I did.
No support line, weaponised incompetence in the app and eventually new help requests were closed right away. I've heard this happened to plenty of people. It stung to lose $500 but chasing it up with uber was worse.
[Pacify] Wait, so their reasoning is for not paying out is because you already had a normal uber account?
How on earth could that make any sense, basically everyone would have an uber account before they ever considered doing deliveries or driving
[ftwmate] yep, exact same thing happend to me.
customer service was no help aswell its a legit a (profanity) scam.
[mr_asstight] We imported a million uber drivers how come more are still needed?
[ozbdssll] Expect that number to drop soon.
The unlimited work rights from the COVID 408 visa are gone, student hours are strictly limited to 48h/fortnight, and with the recent ban on onshore visa hopping, the endless supply of temporary visa drivers is drying up fast. Uber is desperate to replace the churn.
[ozbdssll] Add to that the ban on student visa dependants. Masters/VET students can no longer bring partners or add subsequent entrants.
A huge portion of full-time gig drivers were actually spouses on secondary visas subsidising the primary student's degree. That entire shadow labor pipeline has been turned off overnight.
[Sfh1975] When I came to Australia in 2008 as a student, I was surprised at the laxity of rules regarding students' dependants. My wife was able to work full time. When I was in Europe (Belgium and Germany) on a student visa, they didnt allow her any work. Besides, I was only able to apply for her visa after I proved that I lived in a dwelling suitable for two people (sq mts). And the police visited you every time you registered an address with the city authorities or changed it later. Nothing of the sorts here.
Even though I am an immigrant myself, I am glad they are tightening the laws. I have heard some people would fund their (paper) wife to study in Australia while they earn money. They happily part ways after two or so years, each becoming an immigrant themselves. I heard some would even advertise in local newspapers for such paper wives. Which country that is, I leave it to your imagination ;)

[Pacify] Dont know, it shows up at 3k bonus for me.
(ah 3k is for Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast and Perth only)
[Blokeinhisundies] Do you mean can you do do it on your normal car insurance? No. You're normal insurance won't cover you as you are now using your vehicle for commercial purposes.
[CptnObvious] What insurance do people buy? Any recommendations for company?
[Blokeinhisundies] I haven't done Uber so can't recommend any provider but Uber themselves offer partnered insurance and pretty much all the major insurers offer rideshare insurance.
[chrismheath] You can use "normal" insurance in the sense its the same as others, you just have to specify that you're using partially for commercial purposes. It'll push the price up, depending how much of your driving is commercial vs personal.
If you do rideshare on personal, non-commercial insurance and have an accident, I'm guessing all insurance providers won't cover you and you'll be left to foot the whole bill
[CptnObvious] @chrismheath: I'm reading about Uber's xcover. For those who know, is that pay as you drive and what do people think of it?

[chrismheath] @MrZ: I presume they may have ways of finding out additional details. If you say "no I don't provide ridesharing" and have a crash while doing said thing, you're essentially committing insurance fraud so I guess good luck with that lol

[ihbh] I'd advice against this gig
I'd advise you against giving grammatical advice.

[Pacify] If you live in the $3k bonus zone (Adelaide, Brisbane, Gold Coast and Perth), it doesn't seem like a terrible idea if you got some spare time.
Costs to get going:
Say $150 for medical, $90 PTD, $50 police clearance.
$300 set up fees. Then hire a car for 1 week for $200-300.
So optimistically $2500 profit from bonus if you can hit 100 rides in a week or weekend, depending on your availability.
Now whether that is worth the effort, who knows lol
[urbancartel] Don't think you'll be able to hire a ride-share ready car for that amount - also what's the hire-car running on? Not sure if you've noticed but petrol is around $2.50 a litre

Yeah, sure you got petrol costs - but you also have the actual fares you get from rides lol
[ribze1] Here's the impact of the drop in immigration.
[Fishballs] A lot of people talking negative about this seem to be about human ubering. Is there similar negative for doing uber eats. Do you also need to change insurance if doing uber eats delivering food?
[Realbargainer] It’s modern-day slavery/ forced labour, where sometimes you can't even earn the minimum wage. Whenever I take an Uber, I tend to talk to drivers and understand their perspective. Uber doesn’t always show drivers the destination or how much they will earn before accepting a ride. They only find out how much they’ve earned after dropping off the passenger.
Uber takes nearly 35–40% in fees in some cases (27.5% commission, booking fees and other charges). Drivers also aren’t paid for the time and distance spent travelling to pick up passengers.
Many drivers seem to do this job because they have limited alternatives, not simply because they enjoy the flexibility. I normally tip drivers in cash because I feel they deserve a fairer share.
[MrZ] Not only aren't we paid for time spent travelling to pick up the passenger, but the first 2 minutes of waiting for the passenger aren't paid either. Nor is the time spent, after dropping off the passenger, driving all the way back to the city where all the fares are. Nor are we paid for unexpected traffic jams, like if bad traffic makes your journey 5-10 minutes longer than originally anticipated, you aren't paid for that extra time.
[Realbargainer] I heard some drivers are getting trips more than 10 km away (I would assume atleast 15 minutes pickup time) and with these petrol price and unpaid. And they mentioned that, they get even penalised for not picking that trip based on some rates. This is more than modern slavery.
[muzzamo] Uber say that the fare that is charged does take into account the pickup distance.
https://help.uber.com/en-AU/driving-and-delivering/article/u…
I’d always assumed this was the case and the algorithm sorts it out but just isn’t very transparent about it.

[rrrrrrein] Yes - You can choose which vehicle you will use for Uber Eats delivery upon signing up, including bike.
[Skinnerr] Multiple separate reports on the uber subreddit about these promo's not being honoured. Maybe time for a class action about bait advertising against Uber? Because this, tipping culture and other seppo crap is subversion or, a subtle takeover, of Australia's very hard fought labour laws.

[Eeples] Skilled workers don’t just magically appear especially in places in which loud voices are anti-immigrant.
[WwDesi] Not sure how true but with EBike you can make $2k per week
[MrZ] So, I've been an Uber driver for 10 years now and I'm thinking of quitting very soon. Main reason is that what I'm earning now is no better than what I was making 10 years ago - the pay hasn't gone up at all. In some cases I'm making less, because there are fewer surges. If you're in the outer suburbs, you get paid a much lower rate than you do in the inner city (tiered pricing), whereas previously it was the same rate everywhere. When I first started, a lot of people would sit in the front and talk to you, but now, after COVID, everyone sits in the back which isn't conducive to conversation. Almost nobody gives tips anymore. If someone gets sick in your car or makes a mess, Uber no longer automatically give you a cleaning fee like they used to do. You now have to provide proof/receipt of a professional cleaning service.
The airport trips are especially bad. Every morning I'll get dozens of pre-booked airport requests, some offering me as low as $35, which for me is a 70km, 1 hour round trip with over $20 worth of tolls! Yet, if I go on the Uber app as a passenger, and try to book an airport trip at that time, it shows me $70! So where it the money going? Just not worth it at all.
[Pacify] Wow, $35 for a 70km airport trip is wild
[arkie0] It's dynamic pricing on both the driver side and passenger side - They will offer the driver the bare minimum profit that you are or other drivers are willing to accept, they will have a profiles all their drivers and understand what you're willing to do or not do, both individually and as a group.
Then they do the same on the passenger side, so it maximises profit on both ends
[Sfh1975] This sounds like a race to the bottom. Only if the capitalist world hadnt gotten rid of unions and hadnt hijacked labour parties!
[tenpercent] Unions have been corrupt and failures in supporting their members' interests for decades.
[meowsers] You pay the toll, Uber pays it back in full on top of your fare, and there’s no service fee taken from it. So you end up covered for the tolls.
This is australia we dont tip. They of course dont pay tolls for you to get to the ride.
For me an Uber ride is not a place for conversation. Majority of the time I am hoping my driver doesn't drive like a lunatic, doesn't talk on the phone (or even worse sit on an open line while driving me), or smell / smoke. Also for some reason the new trend of keeping the temp at 26 and A/C off has taken hold. God help us.
The money is probably going to Uber as profit.
[MrZ] The toll is included in the fare - it's not added on. This means that after paying the $12.77 toll to get to the airport, I'm left with a little over $22. This is way below minimum wage.
[Sfh1975] Uber was never meant to be a career. Its essentially a paid car sharing scheme. No one graduated or got trained as an Uber driver. I am extremely sorry the way I sound but what else did you expect from a job that doesnt need education or training? Leave it to the students and part-timers and do something that makes use of your education and training. As I said, I am sorry but this is the hard truth.

[MrZ] @Sfh1975: Easier said than done when you're 45 and your education/qualifications are from 20 years ago.
[meowsers] Included in the fare for the rider. The driver sees their net earnings on the offer.
If you drive through tolls (or not) they are totally separate. Basically tolls don’t matter to you because they are reimbursed directly by the rider.
